headline: Generative models predict perturbation responses and infer dynamics from single-cell snapshots
label: Single Cell Perturbation And Dynamics
summary: Flow matching, disentangled VAEs and language-linked foundation models now target unseen perturbations, while OT and physics priors recover dynamics from snapshots.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative prediction of single-cell perturbation responses. GFM couples knowledge graphs with latent flow matching to predict responses to unseen Perturb-seq perturbations. PertVI disentangles mitotic phase, cell state, batch and treatment effects. scBIG++ predicts full-gene responses to genetic and chemical perturbations using gene-module clustering. LingoCell links single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with language for in silico perturbation. A second line infers dynamics from static data. COATI applies unbalanced synchronized optimal transport to reconstruct coupled scRNA and scATAC trajectories across held-out stages. PhysInfer uses a physics-constrained network to estimate burst size and frequency from static scRNA-seq. scSLIDE (Cell) orders samples along disease trajectories via density-based sample embeddings in Seurat v6. Joint multimodal embeddings appear in scHiR (scRNA-seq with scHi-C) and Bloom (expression with accessibility in mouse brain). Spatial work covers 3D reconstruction (HIM-INR, THiRST) and imputation or domain parsing (SpaAxFormer, CroSP). scDeepSim provides controllable simulation for benchmarking.
